draft.title: Finding a voice
card: Voice is the sense of a particular person speaking in a piece of writing. It comes from choices a writer makes again and again, not from one striking line.
Diction
the words chosen. Slang, formal terms or plain words each suggest a different speaker.
Rhythm
the pattern of sentence length and sound. Short, clipped sentences feel different from long, winding ones.
Attitude
the speaker's stance towards the subject, such as wry, angry, tender or doubtful. When these choices stay consistent, the voice is distinct and a reader is more likely to trust the speaker.
draft.remember: A voice is built from repeated choices in diction, rhythm and attitude.

a.q: Which choice would best help a writer build a consistent voice?
opts: Keeping a steady style of diction, rhythm and attitude
Changing the speaker's style in every paragraph
Using one very unusual word near the start
Copying the style of a famous author exactly
a.why: Voice comes from choices repeated across a piece, so consistency lets the reader recognise one speaker. One unusual word is a single choice, so it cannot build a voice on its own.
a.clue: Think about what makes a speaker sound like the same person throughout.

b.q: A student's speech opens with three very short, blunt sentences in a row. Which feature of voice do the short sentences mainly show?
opts: Rhythm
Diction
Attitude
Audience
b.why: The pattern of sentence length is rhythm. Diction is tempting, but it is about which words are chosen, not how long the sentences are.
b.clue: Focus on how long the sentences are, not on which words are used.

a.best: Keeping a steady style of diction, rhythm and attitude

problems.detail: The clue tells students to focus on 'how long the sentences are', which is the card's definition of rhythm almost word for word. It gives the answer away rather than prompting thought.

check.summary: The card and both answers are correct. The clue for question b nearly states the answer by pointing straight at sentence length, so it should be softened.
